title: Non-blocking follow-ups from PR #127 review (frontend-stock-detail-metric-help)
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #127 (frontend-stock-detail-metric-help), recorded here per CLAUDE.md's 'every non-blocking finding becomes a tracked task' rule so they aren't lost once that PR merges. None of these blocked the PR on their own -- the review's blocking finding (an inaccurate Trigger current-value interpretation) is tracked directly on the parent task instead, since it sent that PR back to implementing.

checklist.step: common/MetricHelp's trigger uses a hardcoded static `data-testid="metric-help-icon"`, but MetricHelp is instantiated ~16 times on a single StockDetailPage render (5 in IndicatorsPanel, 4 in ScreensPanel, up to 7 in SignalSummary including per-breakdown-row). A future test querying `getByTestId('metric-help-icon')` to target one specific metric's icon will hit a 'multiple elements found' (vitest/Testing Library) or Playwright strict-mode violation, or silently grab the wrong instance. Drop the testid (the unique `triggerAriaLabel`-derived aria-label already supports querying by accessible name/role) or derive it per-instance (e.g. via `useId()`, the same pattern InfoBalloon already uses for its own `popoverId`).

No call-site-level tests were added for SignalSummary.tsx/ScreensPanel.tsx/IndicatorsPanel.tsx confirming the right MetricHelp opens with the right content when wired with real component props (checklist item 6 on the parent task claims this done). Only common/MetricHelp itself (MetricHelp.test.tsx) and the content registry's interpretValue functions (metricHelpContent.test.ts) are directly unit-tested; the three panel components reach 100% coverage only via pre-existing renders that happen to mount the new MetricHelp instances, not via a new test that clicks a wired icon and asserts the right metric's content appears. Add at least one such test per panel (e.g. click the EMA13 corner icon in IndicatorsPanel and assert the EMA13-specific text renders, not a different metric's).

tideHelp.interpretValue's Neutral-case message (metricHelpContent.ts) unconditionally states 'the weekly slope and EMA13/26 relationship disagree', but per backend/app/signals/triple_screen.py's evaluate_tide, NEUTRAL can also arise from a genuinely flat/ambiguous slope alone (not necessarily the slope actively disagreeing with the EMA relationship) -- the same family of inaccuracy as the blocking Trigger finding on the parent task, but much lower-impact since the dynamic slope label ('flat') is still shown alongside it. Tighten the wording to cover the flat-slope case accurately (e.g. branch on `weekly_macd_histogram_slope === 'flat'` the same way triggerHelp will need to branch on tide after its fix).
